focus.jnote: The macro tail is dominated by a scheduled event today: CPI at 8:30 AM ET. US stocks are set for a cautious, slightly positive open, with the entire mood hanging on inflation, as investors weigh hotter year-ahead price expectations from the Michigan survey against a packed CPI release. Economists polled by Reuters estimated headline inflation accelerated to an annual 3.6% in September, with core CPI rising 0.2% on a monthly basis. New York Fed President John Williams said the Fed may need to raise its policy rate once more this year to slow inflation, but that he sees no need for hikes in 2027. Meanwhile a chip selloff is extending into a third session — S&P 500 futures were up 0.2%, while an exchange-traded fund tracking chipmakers signaled the sector's five-day selloff was set to continue. Oil is elevated (the current price of Crude Oil WTI futures is 94.58, with a previous close of 94.14) and the 10Y sits near 5.20%. The scanner boarded three bearish post-earnings gaps into this — validate all hard at 9:35.

But shorting into a CPI-day VIX risk with ultra-thin confirming volume is exactly the blow-up 4-VAL exists to prevent. setups.read: Bank of America (BAC) is the scanner's top-graded boarded gap — a bearish Type A at Grade A+. The bank reported EPS of 91 cents (which may not compare with a $1.10 LSEG estimate) on revenue of $30.12 billion versus a $30.69 billion estimate; excluding a $1.2 billion Treasury penalty, EPS would have been $1.08. Shares fell more than 4% in premarket trading (toward ~$51.3 from Tuesday's ~$53.96 close, a ~4.9% gap down). Three honest cautions (voiced here, not by dropping the row): (1) relative volume is ~0.03x — far below the 1.3x confirmation bar, the single biggest red flag; (2) the options-implied move was ~2.9% but the realized gap is ~4.9%, an overshoot that can mean-revert, especially since the adjusted EPS actually cleared ex-fine; (3) there are 3 S/R layers within 7% — swing ~$52.50, gap floor ~$53.96, swing ~$54.65 — so there is cover behind the short strike. Liquidity passes (OI 628, ATM spread $0.17). Next earnings ~Jan 2027 is outside DTE. On a CPI-day RED tape this is strictly 4-VAL-at-9:35 territory — quarter size, skip if it reclaims green.
setups.check_note: Bearish 4-VAL at 9:35: need price < $53.96 (gap holding down), < today's open, and in the lower third of range. Volume ~0.03x is WAY below the 1.3x bar — the key disqualifier; the gap is largely a one-off $1.2B fine, so ex-charge the quarter beat — a snap-back is a real risk. Short call above the ~$53.96 gap floor; size down hard, skip if volume stays thin, it opens green, or CPI jolts the tape.

setups.read: Fastenal (FAST) is a bearish Type A at Grade A — and it's counter-intuitive, because the print was a beat. Q3 revenue was $2.46 billion vs $2.44 billion expected (15.5% YoY growth, a 1% beat), and GAAP EPS of $0.35 was 3.9% above consensus. The market seemed to be hoping for more, and the stock traded down 3.1% to $49.84 immediately after reporting. That's a “sell the news” fade on a rich valuation (~40x forward) rather than a fundamental miss. Honest cautions: (1) relative volume ~0.01x is extraordinarily thin — nowhere near the 1.3x bar; (2) shorting a company that beat is a bet the de-rating continues; (3) there are 4 S/R layers within 7% (swing ~$49.01, sma20 ~$50.28, gap floor ~$51.43, swing ~$52.15), which is cover but also means price is wedged in a tight structure. No OI data returned — verify the chain manually; ATM spread $0.15 is fine. Next earnings ~Jan 2027 is outside DTE. On a RED CPI day, 4-VAL-at-9:35 only — quarter-to-half size, skip if it reclaims green.

setups.read: State Street (STT) is a bearish Type A at Grade B — the sharpest gap of the three but the weakest structure. Non-GAAP EPS of $3.69 was in line with consensus, while revenue of $4.00 billion (up 12.9% YoY) missed the $4.04 billion estimate by about 0.9%. The premarket move was down about 8.8%, even though the monthly decline of about 6% was already running ahead of shorter windows — a repositioning event, not a pure response to the numbers. The stock traded down 6.9% to $162.04 immediately after reporting. Honest cautions: (1) relative volume ~0.02x — again far below 1.3x; (2) the scanner flags NO S/R layers within 7% of price — nothing between the stock and a short strike, which is exactly why this grades B not A; (3) an in-line-EPS, small-rev-miss fade this large (~8%) is prone to a bounce. No OI data returned — verify manually; ATM spread $0.10 passes. Next earnings ~Jan 2027 is outside DTE. On a RED CPI day with no S/R cover, this is the hardest of the three to justify — 4-VAL-at-9:35, minimum size, lean toward skip.

risks: CPI at 8:30 AM ET — the day's dominant, scheduled catalyst. Economists estimated headline inflation accelerated to an annual 3.6% in September, with core CPI rising 0.2% on a monthly basis. A hot print stacked on $95 oil would be the worst-case macro combination.

Chip / semiconductor selloff — an ETF tracking chipmakers signaled the sector's five-day selloff was set to continue. A third-plus day of weakness is dragging Nasdaq futures and could spill into the broad tape.

Fed-hike risk — New York Fed President John Williams said the Fed may need to raise its policy rate once more this year. Ahead of CPI, investors priced in a near 22% chance of a quarter-point US rate hike next week, the CME FedWatch Tool showed.

Single-stock earnings gaps on thin volume — BAC, FAST and STT all gapped on sub-0.03x relative volume; State Street's ~8.8% premarket drop on an in-line result looks partly like a repositioning event rather than a pure response to the numbers, meaning any of these fades can snap back.
Strait of Hormuz / oil — Brent is still above $100 on tanker-attack risk; WTI futures are near $94.58. Any escalation sends crude (and inflation fear) vertical into an already hot CPI backdrop.
